rationale: Continuous safety monitoring has a budget of ~43 minutes left, so rather than stopping at the first question this starts an exploratory run for the other axis: whether the snapshot's protective mechanisms hold the core safety invariants when elections, message loss, partition changes, proposals and leader transfers occur concurrently in real three-node state machines with in-memory storage. Two seeds were explored at 300 steps each. No invariant monitor observed a violation, so this is a bounded negative with an explicit search scope, not a positive finding; it is submitted as exploration with no fixed requirement, and it exercises the deterministic finding's environment for conflicting safety behaviour.

investigations.question: With loss, partition changes, elections, proposals and leader transfers interleaved in a real three-node group, do the captured decision and authority mechanisms keep at most one leader per term, keep applied entries immutable and identical for the same index across nodes, keep the committed index monotonic per node, and keep every previously applied entry present in the log of a node that becomes leader?
investigations.hypothesis: The captured quorum tallying and commit rules should hold these invariants; the exploration looks for any interleaving of ticks, loss, partitions, campaigns, proposals and transfers in which one of them fails, which would be a candidate safety defect rather than an expectation violation.
investigations.discriminator: Per seed, drive three real raft state machines with in-memory storage for 300 steps of random ticks, random connectivity masks, per-message drop decisions, random proposals, campaigns and transfer requests, applying committed entries to a per-node monitor and checking, after every step, one leader per term, unchanged applied entries per index per node, identical entries for the same index across nodes, monotonic committed index, and completeness of every previously applied entry in the log of a state machine that reports itself leader.

scope.description: Exploration with no fixed requirement: three real raft state machines (ids 1,2,3, ElectionTick 10, HeartbeatTick 1, in-memory storage whose ConfState is {1,2,3}) driven for 300 steps per seed, with random connectivity masks that change the reachable peers, per-message drop decisions, random ticks, random proposals from members, random campaigns and random leader transfer requests. Committed entries are applied through the captured log interface, and safety monitors run after every step: one leader per term, applied entries immutable per node and index, identical entry for the same index across nodes, committed index monotonic per node, and every previously applied entry present in the log of a state machine that reports itself leader. Events report any violation with seed, invariant and detail, and one summary per seed with the exercised counts.
assumptions: Messages are delivered in random batches of up to three per step and may be dropped, which models lossy, reordering-prone transport without permanent partitions.
The confinement masks change independently per node, so asymmetric partitions occur.
Entries are persisted to the in-memory storage through the captured helpers before messages are delivered, matching the documented usage.
No configuration changes are injected in this exploration; membership transitions are covered by the deterministic experiments.
excluded: Membership changes, snapshot transfer and restart recovery (covered by deterministic experiments or left for later)
Crash-stop faults: state machines keep running for the whole scenario
Any claim of absence of defects beyond the two explored seeds and 300 steps each

experiment.prefix: For each seed in {11, 23}: create three raft state machines with in-memory storage whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3}. Then loop 300 steps; each step may change the per-node reachability masks, tick some state machines, step a random proposal on a member, step a random campaign, step a random leader transfer request, collect outbound messages (dropping those between unreachable peers or per a random drop decision), shuffle and deliver at most three messages, then persist and apply committed entries and run the safety monitors, emitting a violation event for each monitor failure and a summary event per seed at the end.
